This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 30.01.2023 at about 11.45 a.m. he had been riding two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JG-8584 on Inner Ring Road, near Srinivagilu, Ejipura Signal,
Bengaluru, at that time, a driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-9230 has parked his car on main road in no parking zone and negligently opened his right side door without observing movement of the vehicles, as a result the door of the car hit to the two wheeler of the petitioner and caused accident, due to the impact,he has sustained bleeding injuries over face, head injury and injury to abdomen and chest and his motor cycle is also damaged.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.7,00,000/- towards SCCH-5 hospitalization, conveyance, medical expenses and other incidental charges.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 39 years, hale and healthy, working as multi-tasking staff as M/s.United Facility Management Services, Bengaluru thereby drawing salary of Rs.20,000/-
p.m.
due to this accident, petitioner is still under treatment and could not resume to his avocation.
Out of this accident crime No.15/2023 is registered against the driver of the said car before the Ashoknagar Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. SCCH-5 4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared, but not filed written statement.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement.
Further submited that, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, petitioner has registered case against driver of the car by name Mr.Raju, but in police authorities have filed charge sheet against car driver by name Raja P., petitioner has filed false case against the driver of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-AC-9230.
Further denied existence of insurance policy in respect of said car and if there is any liability, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied occurrence of the accident and involvement of alleged vehicle in the accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 30.01.2023 at about 11.45 a.m. near Srinivagilu,
Inner Ring Road, Ejipura Signal,blr due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-AC-9230 dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Senior Technician in Medical Records Department at Manipal Hospitals as PW-2, Dr.Naveen Kumar H.R.
Consultant at SCCH-5 BGS Gleneagles Global Hospitals as PW-3 and marked 20 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 and closed his evidence.

On the other hand, Deputy Manager at respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed evidence.
7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated SCCH-5 in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of notice is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.11.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he has examined Senior Technician at Medical Records Department and Doctor as PW-2 and PW-3.
On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar with skethc, notice, reply, charge Sathish Kumar.
R vs Raja

.P on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103376498/
3 sheet and IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident SCCH-5 dated 30.01.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.
On the other hand, Deputy Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.2.
Further except above evidence, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 30.01.2023 at about 11.45 a.m. when he was riding two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JG-8584 on Inner Ring Road, near Srinivagilu, Ejipura Signal, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by SCCH-5 the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-9230.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained injury to face, right side chest and abdomen.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Mnaipal Hospitals, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since SCCH-5 30.01.2023 to 06.02.2023 i.e., for 7 days.

Further he has furnished photographs with CD marked as Ex.P.9 and medical bills amounting to Rs.5,32,207/- marked as Ex.P.10.
13.

To substantiate his case, he has examined Senior Technician in Medical Records Department at Mnaipal Hospitals by name Vedavati N. as PW-2 and exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.13, copy of MLC as Ex.P.14, copy of police intimation as Ex.P.15, IP records marked as Ex.P.16 and CT-Scan Films and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.17.
14.
Further Dr.Naveen Kumar H.R. Consultant at BGS Gleneagles Global Hospitals, Kengeri is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD Book marked as Ex.P.18,
X-ray Films with Report marked as Ex.P.19 and surgery estimation report marked SCCH-5 as Ex.P.20 and he has assessed permanent disability of 24.5% for loss of facial component.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner, but only assessed the disability.
Further deposed that, treatment is under healing process.

Fr deposed that,
there is fixation of 3 lower teeths for which there is light tenderness, after surgery which will take 1 hear to reach normal stage and there is loss of strength to take hard food at the ratio of 45%.
further deposed that, he can do office work.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 9% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body SCCH-5 out of 24.5% loss of facial component disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

4 15.

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 39 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 28.05.1983 and the alleged accident is occurred on 30.01.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 his age is considered about 40 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident,

notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner was admitted in Manipal Hospitals as inpatient from 30.01.2023 to 06.02.2023 i.e., for 7 days.

For the said period he is SCCH-5 entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.15,250/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,558/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
18. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.10 medical bills for Rs.5,32,207/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.R.Shashikanth has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 30.01.2023.

So as per Ex.P.7 wound SCCH-5 certificate, petitioner has sustained blunt injury to chest with 5th to 8th rib fracture right side, blunt injury to abdoment with laceration of thigh periplepabic collection, facial injuries with displaced fracture of nasal bone, displaced fracture bilateral maxilarry, displaced fracture of right zygomatic process, displaced fracture of right orbit,
which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Raja P. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1 to PW-3.
19.
Per contra, except oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to prove the allegations as SCCH-5 alleged in the written statement.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner

are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the Sathish Kumar.R vs Raja.P on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103376498/
5 defence as taken in the written statement.

20. Ofcourse during the course of arguments, Smt.S vehemently argued that, Rs.5,70,000/- medical bills are re-imbursed and petitioner not proved about discharge from the company and about 320 members are working in the said company and he has not wearing helmet and contributory negligence principle attracts in this case etc.,
21.
Per contra, petitioner counsel Sri.SJKR argued that, defence of respondent No.2 is only on assumptions and reimbursement of medical bills not proved etc., SCCH-5

Accordingly arguments of respondent No.2 counsel about avocation of petitioner and his income is considered as discussed above and rest of the arguments have not supports the respondent No.2 case, because not proved the same.

Ofcourse in complaint, the name of accused is mentioned as Raju and charge sheet is filed against Raja as argued by the respondent No.2 counsel, but merely one spelling i.e., Raju and Raja names are mentioned in FIR, complaint and charge sheet are not having much difference as argued by the respondent No.2 counsel.

22. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No

. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of Future Income 2,47,050-00 2. Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges
4. Medical Expenses 5,32,207-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 SCCH-5 6. Loss of income during laid up 3,558-00 period Total 8,27,815-00 23.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,27,815/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.140122323380001080 which is valid for the period from 19.01.2023 to 18.01.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 30.01.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that,
respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of SCCH-5 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

: : ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,27,815/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Twenty Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Fifteen Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept SCCH-5 in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
